facts.raw_span: A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: The patient has bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, which are characteristic findings of blepharitis.
The patient has both lower eyelids that are ectropic, which is a key feature of ectropion.
The patient has diffuse conjunctival hyperemia, which is a common finding in conjunctivitis.
The patient has biopsy-proven Crohn disease, which is a key diagnosis in this case.
The patient developed blepharitis while on infliximab therapy, suggesting a possible association between the two.
The patient continued to have blepharitis after switching to adalimumab, suggesting that the condition may be related to TNF-alpha inhibitor therapy.
The patient has conjunctival hyperemia and blepharitis, which may be related to TNF-alpha inhibitor therapy.
The patient has normal visual acuity and an unremarkable ophthalmic examination, which makes other diagnoses less likely and raises the possibility of normal-tension glaucoma.
The patient has crusty plaques on the eyelid margins and diffuse conjunctival hyperemia, which are common findings in dry eye syndrome.
The patient has bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, which are characteristic findings of meibomian gland dysfunction.
It explains the visual acuity finding in the context of infliximab therapy.

rationales.F04: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids are characteristic of blepharitis.
rationales.F05: Ectropion is a known complication of blepharitis.
rationales.F06: Normal visual acuity suggests that the ocular inflammation is not affecting the patient's vision.
rationales.F07: Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins are a common finding in blepharitis.
rationales.F08: Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia is a sign of conjunctivitis, which can be caused by TNF-alpha inhibitors.
rationales.F09: The absence of other ocular findings suggests that the patient does not have other underlying ocular conditions, such as glaucoma or dry eye syndrome.
